outcomes.title: The inspector knows whether a component forwards className or style before an edit
outcomes.before: The inspector's read facts hard-coded acceptsClassName and acceptsStyle to true. The planner could pick a channel on a custom component that silently drops the prop. A color click then changed nothing and showed no error. The SaaS browser path never called a detector at all.
outcomes.now: A per-channel forward detector (§9.2a, “A1”) now feeds the VS Code and SaaS read paths and the extension's pre-write gate. It traces the component's render body, tells the root element from a descendant, and recognizes asChild/Slot and styled-components wrappers, including one level of styled(Component). A channel counts as not forwarding only on a high-confidence negative.
outcomes.scope: Read and capability slice of §9.2a only.
verification: Tests added in the squash diffs, counted from added `it(`/`test(` lines: #719 85, #734 24, #736 17, #743 10. Suite totals in the commit messages are recorded proof from the authors, not a new run.
These four pull requests have no screenshot, so tests are the only proof.

The detector's algorithm order deliberately differs from the literal §9.2a prose. The spec amendment (HYP-1232) is still todo.
A1 covers the read side. The shared runtime-verify foundation (B1) is still absent.

outcomes.title: A style edit on a component that cannot take the prop is refused and rolled back
outcomes.before: A padding, margin, radius or width edit on a component that did not forward style wrote a dead prop onto it. The DOM stayed the same, nothing rolled back, no warning appeared, and TypeScript reported an error. Two shapes caused it: a component that forwarded className but not style, and one imported from a monorepo workspace package that resolved as external.
outcomes.now: The shared executor checks every channel a write will touch before it mutates anything and returns a structured nonForwarding refusal. outcomes.title: A color edit that cannot find its CSS rule now lands as an inline style
outcomes.before: When the CSS Module or plain CSS rule for an edit could not be located, the executor hard-failed. The color edit did nothing visible and no usable error appeared. The spec called this a dead click.
outcomes.now: On a rule miss the executor writes the declarations onto the source element's own style attribute. It finds the JSX file through the element reference, because the owner's path is the CSS file. It acts only on a plain .class or #id target in the base condition, re-runs the dead-prop forwarding check first, and reports a distinguishable failure if every declaration drops. Conditional, at-rule and combinator targets still fail.

outcomes.title: A delayed edit cannot land on another selection or start AI repair after cancellation
outcomes.boundary: A pre-dispatch guard only. The composed and SaaS interaction matrix (HYP-1481) and the SaaS single-select reread (HYP-1588) are not covered.
outcomes.before: A probe or write that outlived its selection could apply to the next selection or trigger the ordinary write-error AI fallback. After a newer edit, an older failure could leave the inspector showing a value that never reached the file.
outcomes.now: Pending probes are bound to the original bridge, workspace, sub-project, selection occurrence and preview scope, so A→B→A is caught. They are rejected before dispatch with a typed STALE_CANVAS_CONTEXT outcome and an “Edit cancelled” notice, never a generic AI repair. Queued edits are scoped by selected ids, occurrence, pseudo-state and source tab. When the latest edit settles, a source reread repairs the inspector after an older same-scope failure. Hover is deduplicated against the selected occurrences.
outcomes.scope: A bounded pre-dispatch guard. Not Canvas demo sign-off.
verification: Recorded proof (author report, not rerun here): 121 host, RPC, hook and overlay tests pass on a4421822, and a 29 September commit adds 11 hook regressions that fail on the previous source.

The pull request body has two screenshots from a real VS Code run in an isolated profile: the “Edit cancelled” notice with the source unchanged, and the next ordinary edit persisting. They are two stages of one run, and annotated crops of both are shown above.
caveats: The full composed and SaaS interaction matrix and hover-exit parity remain open under HYP-1481. HYP-1588 leaves SaaS single-select without the reread.
The pull request is stacked on an open branch and its merge gates are unchecked.

quotes.text: The shared RPC/Inspector path preserves cancellation as a typed outcome instead of invoking the ordinary write-error AI fallback.
The guard ends at dispatch; it is not a guarantee that an already-running mutation has document-level CAS or cancelable commit.
quotes.note: The spec states the limit. The paragraph was written by the same author as the candidate.

outcomes.title: A Canvas drag-move is proven by the preview, and rolled back when wrong
outcomes.boundary: Review changes were requested on an earlier head, and the branch conflicts with its base. Undo and Redo of a move are not render-verified (HYP-1539).
outcomes.before: The runtime had no drop verification. A successful API reply, a changed file or a non-empty diff could be reported as success, and a failed move stayed on disk behind an optional Undo button. An earlier approach trusted hot-reload events, which Vite 6.4.1 can emit even when the import was rejected.
outcomes.now: A drag writes temporary data-hc-moveid markers at positions taken from the syntax tree, without reprinting the file or adding a wrapper. The preview reads the committed fibers carrying the markers. The move counts as verified only with exactly one carrier per marker, unchanged content, the requested order in fibers, DOM and layout, no portal, and the outline on the moved element. One owned compare-and-swap write then commits the unmarked image. On failure the markers are restored, the restore echo is awaited and the move is rolled back. An order drop edits only the order-* token across every affected file in one undo batch.
outcomes.scope: Move and order-drop paths in VS Code.
verification: Recorded proof on 4c7bcb0e (author report, not rerun here): application 8,103 pass and 0 fail, native packages 913 and 0, changed extension suites 199 and 0. `bun run test` exits 1 only because of a state-lib site gate in files the pull request does not touch. A route control for HYP-1541 fails on a mutant that reloads before every restore echo.

The pull request body embeds nine screenshots from an installed VS Code: the drag outline and result, a restore after a failed module, typing 0.8 s and 0.2 s after a drop, a selection change mid-move, and an order drop before and after. The order drop before and after, and the restore notice, are shown above as annotated crops; the other images are not reproduced.
caveats: The pull request has a CHANGES_REQUESTED review on an earlier head and conflicts with its base.
Undo and Redo of a move are not render-verified (HYP-1539). Clicking the editor tab while a move is checked undoes the move (HYP-1599); #819 carries the fix.
The spec says of these paragraphs that they are a proposal pending its Part owner's re-sign. Data-owner reorder adapters for API, database or virtualized lists are not covered.

quotes.text: Failure to resolve or a verification timeout is **unverified**, never success.
Compensate the exact operation by identifier and owned after-images; never call “Undo latest” because a newer independent operation may already be on top.
Reorder the source of order, not an arbitrary array index.

outcomes.boundary: Render-verified Undo and Redo, complete SaaS and occurrence acceptance, and real-OS hover are not covered.

outcomes.title: Style Editor operation authority: a stale write result cannot publish after the context ends
outcomes.boundary: The pull request conflicts with main. Live extension and SaaS acceptance and HYP-1588 are separate work, and no latency, memory or size win is claimed.
outcomes.before: Late write results could still publish feedback after the selection changed or the panel unmounted. In the earlier pilot (#824) three late-error scenarios stayed red under both the React baseline and the state-lib arm, so the problem was in the app's ownership of requests, not in the state container.
outcomes.now: #827 gives the shared useStyleSync hook one revocable operation scope per committed editor context. When the context ends, through a new selection, an A→B→A return or an unmount, the scope is revoked. Stale feedback is dropped and a retained input handler can no longer enqueue a write. A read-only lease keeps the source-reread obligation. The writer, planner, rollback and journal stay where they were.
outcomes.scope: Operation authority in one hook. Not a state-lib migration of the Style Editor.
verification: A real VS Code 1.124.2 extension write changed the fixture's `w-12` to `w-[140px]`, and the preview width became 140 px after hot reload (pair above). It proves that an ordinary write still settles. It does not test stale responses or rollback.

Recorded proof (author report, not rerun here): with only the library guard removed, 2 of 4 real-hook tests fail. Stale-response behavior is checked in a browser fixture built from the real right sidebar with a simulated extension host, so it is a fixture result, not acceptance in the live editor.
Recorded proof (author report, not rerun here): 7,975 application tests pass with 7 existing skips, and 1,086 package tests pass.
caveats: The pull request is open and conflicts with main. Its own report says no latency, memory, code-size or adoption win is claimed, so there is no shipped speedup.
The #805 policy is inherited by #827, not claimed again. Live extension and SaaS acceptance and HYP-1588 are separate requirements.

outcomes.statusLabel: Measured on fixtures · open pull requests · not a product speedup
outcomes.title: Measured pilot: no proven speedup, and one real bug found
outcomes.before: The adoption document (§2, item 4) expected per-control inspector updates without re-render storms and said to verify that. The pilot asked whether a state library would make typing faster, cut re-renders or shrink the Style Editor code.
outcomes.now: The #824 pilot ran the same Style Editor scenarios against the React baseline and against state-lib through one test-visible backend switch: typing was equal (median 29.5 ms against 29.6 ms, author report), the bundle and the glue code grew, and the report records a no-go for wider adoption. The #828 to #831 stack then compared state-lib with an equally protected native version. It found one real bug: a failed 130 px write could open the AI fallback while the newer 140 px value still waited for debounce. The fix is in #830, which is open. #831 localizes inspector subscriptions: per 1,000 edits the root panel is called 13 times instead of 1,013, and main-thread CPU falls from 1,315 ms to 800 ms in a controlled fixture. An equally localized native version reaches 831 ms, and the right webview grows by 2,404 bytes gzip.
outcomes.scope: Measurement on fixtures. No performance gain is shipped.
verification: All numbers come from a controlled fixture built from the real right sidebar with a simulated host transport. Chromium and Node ran on a shared host, and the capture-to-second-frame time only approximates interaction latency. Live AST and hot reload are not exercised.
Recorded proof (author report, not rerun here): #830 hook tests went from 45 pass and 1 fail to 46 pass; in a browser probe the old bundle sent one stale AI command and the new bundle sent none.
The bench screenshots in these pull requests are fixture captures, and three of the field-subscription images are byte-identical, so none is shown in this report as the editor.
caveats: Not proven: input speed-up, fewer re-renders than an equally localized native version, smaller total integration code, a smaller bundle. Multi-selection still uses sequential field setters.
All five pull requests are open and stacked, and #831 has no passing check at its stacked head. HYP-1536 acceptance, including the Hyper-wide gate, is unchecked.
